column2: Which term names the object, surface, or viewpoint used as the comparison for motion?
column4: acceleration

column2: A phone stays on a bus seat. Relative to the seat, the phone is
column4: at rest

column2: The same phone is moving relative to
column4: the bus floor

column2: Which everyday frame is usually implied when a runner’s speed is reported?
column4: the runner’s shirt

column2: Which statement explicitly includes a reference frame?
column3: The cart is at rest relative to the platform.
column4: The cart moves fast.

column2: A drone stays over one point on a moving boat. Which pair of descriptions can both be correct?
column3: moving relative to boat and at rest relative to shore
column4: at rest relative to boat and moving relative to shore
column6: moving at the same speed in every frame

column2: Why can two observers disagree about whether a suitcase is moving without either being wrong?
column4: One observer measures time differently because of mass.
column5: They may use different reference frames.
column6: Every object has two positions at once.

column2: Which revision best fixes “The passenger is not moving”?
column3: The passenger is not really moving.
column4: The passenger is not moving anywhere.
column5: The passenger is at rest relative to all objects.
column6: The passenger is at rest relative to the bus seat.

column2: A classroom desk is at rest relative to the floor but moves with Earth around the Sun. What idea does this illustrate?
column4: speed is always constant

column2: For describing a person walking inside a train, which frame would best show the person’s motion through the aisle?
column4: the train floor

column2: Observer A rides on a cart and says a box is at rest. Observer B stands beside the track and says it is moving. Which evaluation is best?
column3: Observer A must be wrong because the cart moves.
column4: Observer B must be wrong because the box does not slide.
column5: Both can be correct because each compares the box with a different frame.
column6: The box must switch between rest and motion.

column2: A student says there is one “true” answer to whether an object moves. Which response is strongest?
column3: The answer is always based on Earth.
column4: The answer is always based on the moving object.
column6: The answer depends on the stated reference frame, so the claim is incomplete.

column2: A rider sits on a subway. Which statement can be true?
column3: at rest relative to seat and moving relative to station
column4: moving relative to seat and at rest relative to station
column5: at rest relative to every frame
column6: moving relative to every frame at the same speed

column2: Which example best shows one object using two reference frames?
column4: a backpack compared with a train seat and a platform

column2: Which phrase identifies the frame in “The cyclist is moving relative to the road”?
column4: moving

column2: A moving walkway carries a standing traveler. Relative to the walkway the traveler is at rest; relative to the floor the traveler is moving. This means
column3: the traveler has no real motion
column4: the floor is not a valid frame
column6: rest is relative to the chosen frame

column2: Which observer most naturally uses the ground as a reference frame?
column3: a spectator beside a race track
column4: a passenger seated on a train
column5: a person standing on a moving walkway

column2: What should be added first to the statement “The book moved 2 m” to make it a clearer motion description?
column4: the reference frame

column2: Two videos show different motion for the same passenger, one from inside a bus and one from a building. Which explanation fits?
column4: The passenger changes mass between videos.
column5: The cameras are fixed to different reference frames.

column2: Which statement about Earth’s surface is correct?
column3: It is the only frame allowed in physics.
column4: It is at rest relative to every object.
column5: It makes all moving objects have the same speed.
column6: It is a convenient common frame for everyday nearby motion, not the only valid frame.
